searchText: <@!88765147048333312> is there a way to union types in open rpc? for example (in typescript) `{one: string, two: string} && ( {three: string} || {four: string})` which is to say it's either `{one, two, three}` or `{one, two, four}` this is particularly useful for 1559 changes which will add a new return type while not deleting the previous I suppose we could just say that the old is old is just standard and new is 1559 or something Yes, I looked into it a while back and found it was possible. Something like `anyOf` I thinik. Oh, sorry, `anyOf` is union, but you want intersection. such as `oneOf`? No, that is a weird thing. It is a union, bet it doesn't support subsets. I don't actually know why you would ever use it instead of `anyOf`. `allOf` I think is what you want. `allOf({one, two}, anyOf({three},{four}))` oh okay cool do you have the documentation at hand? Nope. Just examples. <https://github.com/open-rpc/examples/blob/master/service-descriptions/petstore-expanded-openrpc.json> That one uses `allOf` in it, I think one of the other examples uses `anyOf`. weird, looks like the docs don't have much on it (from a cursory look) <@!88765147048333312> do you know about this at all? Okay, I can use it, then / figure it out They have a Discord server, may be worth asking in there to see if someone can give a quick answer. Ah, they are part of JSON Schema, not OpenRPC. <https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/combining.html> oh nice find, thanks wouldn't it just be oneOf though? becuase if you did anyOf then that'd say you could have the removed + added stuff on the transaction so oneOf would presumably prevent that, no? `oneOf` would work in place of `anyOf` there, but not always. Hmm, actually I see what you are saying now. If someone sent `{one, two, three, four}`, that would match `allOf({one, two}, anyOf({three},{four}))` but it would not make sense. OK, I'm convinced that `oneOf` is right here. <@!301186049323958275> updated PR https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/47

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: <@!88765147048333312> is there a way to union types in open rpc? for example (in typescript) `{one: string, two: string} && ( {three: string} || {four: string})` which is to say it's either `{one, two, three}` or `{one, two, four}`

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: this is particularly useful for 1559 changes which will add a new return type while not deleting the previous

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: I suppose we could just say that the old is old is just standard and new is 1559 or something

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Yes, I looked into it a while back and found it was possible.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Something like `anyOf` I thinik.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Oh, sorry, `anyOf` is union, but you want intersection.

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: such as `oneOf`?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: No, that is a weird thing.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: It is a union, bet it doesn't support subsets.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I don't actually know why you would ever use it instead of `anyOf`.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: `allOf` I think is what you want.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: `allOf({one, two}, anyOf({three},{four}))`

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: oh okay cool

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: do you have the documentation at hand?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Nope.  Just examples.  <https://github.com/open-rpc/examples/blob/master/service-descriptions/petstore-expanded-openrpc.json>

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: That one uses `allOf` in it, I think one of the other examples uses `anyOf`.

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: weird, looks like the docs don't have much on it (from a cursory look) <@!88765147048333312> do you know about this at all?

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: Okay, I can use it, then / figure it out

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: They have a Discord server, may be worth asking in there to see if someone can give a quick answer.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Ah, they are part of JSON Schema, not OpenRPC.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: <https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/combining.html>

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: oh nice find, thanks

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: wouldn't it just be oneOf though?

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: becuase if you did anyOf then that'd say you could have the removed + added stuff on the transaction

excerpts.author: alita85
excerpts.content: so oneOf would presumably prevent that, no?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: `oneOf` would work in place of `anyOf` there, but not always.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Hmm, actually I see what you are saying now.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If someone sent `{one, two, three, four}`, that would match `allOf({one, two}, anyOf({three},{four}))` but it would not make sense.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: OK, I'm convinced that `oneOf` is right here.
